answer.rationale: Write-path p99 has been climbing for 90 minutes while settlement traffic is at its daily peak. The security patch cannot be rolled back, so `rollback_release` is eliminated outright. `regional_failover` moves the whole write plane during peak settlement load and risks losing in-flight customer writes during the cutover. `add_capacity` would help if the problem were raw capacity, but 90 minutes of gradual p99 climbing at peak write load points to read/query work piling onto the primary and contending with writes — the exact pattern memory_b5 records on day 55, where routing report queries to read replicas took dashboard load off the primary and transactional write latency recovered the same day. Verifying memory_b5 is the highest-value single check because it is the closest structural analogue and, if confirmed, `route_read_replicas` is the only intervention that relieves write-path pressure without reverting the mandatory security patch, without shifting regions mid-peak, and without waiting for provisioning. `enable_circuit_breaker` would shed partner traffic but settlement is our own core path, so breaking it would lose customer writes. Therefore: verify memory_b5, then execute a small guarded test — route read/report/dashboard queries to replicas, watch write p99 for 10–15 minutes, and promote only if latency recovers. Fallback if verification fails: escalate to `add_capacity` in the next window while maintaining the patch.
